tips.title: Dry Fitting with a 'Best Fit' Approach
tips.text: Use a combination of visual inspection and feel to identify the optimal position for each part during dry fitting. For example, use a caliper to measure the distance between a part's mounting holes and the corresponding holes in the surrounding structure. This ensures accurate positioning and minimizes the risk of misaligned parts during assembly.

tips.title: Structural Support with Spacers and Dowel Pins
tips.text: When assembling a complex structure, use spacers and dowel pins to maintain precise alignment and prevent distortion. For instance, when joining two parts with a large gap, insert a dowel pin to act as a pivot point, allowing the parts to be aligned accurately. Then, use a spacer to maintain the correct distance between the parts.

tips.title: Modifying Parts with 3D Printing and Milling
tips.text: Use 3D printing to create custom parts or modify existing ones with complex geometries. For example, print a custom adapter to connect two parts with incompatible interfaces. Alternatively, use a CNC milling machine to machine custom holes or profiles on existing parts, allowing for precise alignment and optimal fitment.

tips.title: Seam Filling with Epoxy and Putty
tips.text: When filling seams, use a combination of epoxy resin and putty to achieve a strong and visually appealing bond. Apply a thin layer of putty to the seam, allowing it to cure before applying multiple thin layers of epoxy. This approach ensures a strong bond, minimal shrinkage, and a smooth finish.

tips.title: Construction Sequencing with a 'Top-Down' Approach
tips.text: When assembling a complex structure, use a 'top-down' approach to construction sequencing. Start by assembling the uppermost components, working your way down to the base. This approach allows for easier access to parts, reduces the risk of parts getting damaged, and facilitates the use of temporary supports and clamps.
